arxiv-2004-07393.title: Minimal quantum heat manager boosted by bath spectral filtering
arxiv-2004-07393.creator: M. Tahir Naseem, Avijit Misra, Özgür E. Müstecaplıoğlu, Gershon Kurizki
arxiv-2004-07393.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by M. Tahir Naseem, Avijit Misra, Özgür E. Müstecaplıoğlu, Gershon Kurizki. We reveal the potentially important role of a general mechanism in quantum heat management schemes, namely, spectral filtering of the coupling between the heat baths in the setup and the quantum system that controls the heat flow. Such filtering is enabled by interfaces between the system and the baths by means of harmonic-oscillator modes whose resonant frequencies and coupling strengths are used as control parameters of the system-bath coupling spectra.

arxiv-2101-09904.title: Using Angle of Arrival for Improving Indoor Localization
arxiv-2101-09904.creator: Sai Koppula, Shivang Singh
arxiv-2101-09904.description: Abstract In this paper, we primarily explore the improvement of single stream audio systems using Angle of Arrival calculations in both simulation and real life gathered data. We wanted to learn how to discern the direction of an audio source from gathered signal data to ultimately incorporate into a multi modal security system.

arxiv-2107-03812.title: Convergence of the Neumann-Neumann Method for the Cahn-Hilliard Equation
arxiv-2107-03812.creator: Gobinda Garai 1
arxiv-2107-03812.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Gobinda Garai 1. In this paper, we analyze a substructuring type algorithm for the Cahn-Hilliard (CH) equation. Being a nonlinear equation, it is of great importance to develop efficient numerical schemes for investigating the solution behaviour of the CH equation. We present the formulation of Neumann-Neumann (NN) method applied to the CH equation and investigate the convergence behaviour of the same in one and two spatial dimension for two subdomains. We illustrate the theoretical results by providing numerical example.

arxiv-2109-01416.title: On the inertial range bounds of K-41 like Magnetohydrodynamics turbulence.
arxiv-2109-01416.creator: T.A. Tegegn
arxiv-2109-01416.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by T.A. Tegegn. The spectral slope of Magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) turbulence varies depending on the spectral theory considered; − 3 / 2 -3/2 is the spectral slope in Kraichnan-Iroshnikov-Dobrowolny (KID) theory, − 5 / 3 -5/3 in Marsch-Matthaeus-Zhou’s and Goldreich-Sridhar theories also called Kolmogorov-like (K-41 like) MHD theory, combination of the − 5 / 3 -5/3 and − 3 / 2 -3/2 scales in Biskamp and so on. A rigorous mathematical proof to any of these spectral theories is of great scientific interest.

arxiv-2201-10475.title: Variationally consistent mass scaling for explicit time-integration schemes of lower- and higher-order finite element methods
arxiv-2201-10475.creator: Stein K.F. Stoter, Thi-Hoa Nguyen, René R. Hiemstra, Dominik Schillinger
arxiv-2201-10475.description: Abstract In this paper, we propose a variationally consistent technique for decreasing the maximum eigenfrequencies of structural dynamics related finite element formulations. Our approach is based on adding a symmetric positive-definite term to the mass matrix that follows from the integral of the traction jump across element boundaries.

arxiv-2303-10494.title: Revisiting the Plastic Surgery Hypothesis via Large Language Models
arxiv-2303-10494.creator: Chunqiu Steven Xia, Yifeng Ding, Lingming Zhang
arxiv-2303-10494.description: Abstract . Automated Program Repair (APR) aspires to automatically generate patches for an input buggy program. Traditional APR tools typically focus on specific bug types and fixes through the use of templates, heuristics, and formal specifications. However, these techniques are limited in terms of the bug types and patch variety they can produce.

arxiv-2303-18025.title: Short vs. long range exchange interactions in twisted bilayer graphene
arxiv-2303-18025.creator: Alejandro Jimeno-Pozo, Zachary A. H. Goodwin, Pierre A. Pantaleón, Valerio Vitale, Lennart Klebl, Dante M. Kennes, Arash Mostofi, Johannes Lischner, Francisco Guinea
arxiv-2303-18025.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Alejandro Jimeno-Pozo, Zachary A. H. Goodwin, Pierre A. Pantaleón, Valerio Vitale, Lennart Klebl, Dante M. Kennes, Arash Mostofi, Johannes Lischner, Francisco Guinea. We discuss the effect of long-range interactions within the self-consistent Hartree-Fock (HF) approximation in comparison to short-range atomic Hubbard interactions on the band structure of twisted bilayer graphene (TBG) at charge neutrality for various twist angles.

arxiv-2308-02779.title: Quasiparticle and Transport Properties of Disordered Bilayer Graphene
arxiv-2308-02779.creator: Yanru Chen, Bo Fu, Jinrong Xu, Qinwei Shi, Ping Cui, Zhenyu Zhang
arxiv-2308-02779.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Yanru Chen, Bo Fu, Jinrong Xu, Qinwei Shi, Ping Cui, Zhenyu Zhang. In recent experimental and theoretical studies of graphene, disorder scattering processes have been suggested to play an important role in its electronic and transport properties. In the preceding paper, it has been shown that the nonperturbative momentum-space Lanczos method is able to accurately describe all the multiple impurity scattering events and account for the quasiparticle and transport properties of disordered monolayer graphene.

arxiv-2309-05429.title: Improving Information Extraction on Business Documents with Specific Pre-Training Tasks
arxiv-2309-05429.creator: Thibault Douzon, Stefan Duffner, Christophe Garcia, Jérémy Espinas
arxiv-2309-05429.description: Abstract Transformer-based Language Models are widely used in Natural Language Processing related tasks. Thanks to their pre-training, they have been successfully adapted to Information Extraction in business documents. However, most pre-training tasks proposed in the literature for business documents are too generic and not sufficient to learn more complex structures.

arxiv-2412-02052.title: FoveaSPAD: Exploiting Depth Priors for Adaptive and Efficient Single-Photon 3D Imaging
arxiv-2412-02052.creator: Justin Folden, Atul Ingle *, Sanjeev J. Koppal *
arxiv-2412-02052.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Justin Folden, Atul Ingle *, Sanjeev J. Koppal *. Fast, efficient, and accurate depth-sensing is important for safety-critical applications such as autonomous vehicles. Direct time-of-flight LiDAR has the potential to fulfill these demands, thanks to its ability to provide high-precision depth measurements at long standoff distances. While conventional LiDAR relies on avalanche photodiodes (APDs), single-photon avalanche diodes (SPADs) are an emerging image-sensing technology that offer many advantages such as extreme sensitivity and time resolution.

arxiv-2507-09348.title: Fragments of Some Subintuitionistic Logics
arxiv-2507-09348.creator: Fatemeh Shirmohammadzadeh Maleki
arxiv-2507-09348.description: Abstract In this article we determine the implicational fragments of most of the known subintuitionistic logics. 1 Introduction In a series of papers [ 4 , 5 , 6 , 7 , 12 ] we discussed a number of subintuitionistic logics between WF and IPC .

arxiv-2509-19040.title: Nonparametric efficient estimation of the longitudinal front-door functional
arxiv-2509-19040.creator: Marie S. Breum, Helene C. W. Rytgaard, Torben Martinussen, Erin E. Gabriel
arxiv-2509-19040.description: Abstract The front-door criterion is an identification strategy for the intervention-specific mean outcome in settings where the standard back-door criterion fails due to unmeasured exposure-outcome confounders, but an intermediate variable exists that completely mediates the effect of exposure on the outcome and is not affected by unmeasured confounding.

arxiv-2509-20075.title: Supergiant GCIRS 22 in the Milky Way Nuclear Star Cluster: Revised alpha abundances
arxiv-2509-20075.creator: B. Thorsbro, S. Khalidy, R. M. Rich, M. Schultheis, D. Taniguchi, A. M. Amarsi, G. Kordopatis, G. Nandakumar, S. Nishiyama, N. Ryde
arxiv-2509-20075.description: Abstract Context. The chemical abundances of alpha-elements in Galactic Centre (GC) supergiants provide key insights into the chemical enrichment and star formation history of the Milky Wayś Nuclear Star Cluster. Previous studies have reported enhanced alpha-element abundances, raising questions about the chemical evolution of this unique region. Aims.

arxiv-2511-07949.title: Stabilization of Time-Varying Perturbed Quantum Systems via Reduced Filters
arxiv-2511-07949.creator: Weichao Liang, Daoyi Dong
arxiv-2511-07949.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Weichao Liang, Daoyi Dong. In practical applications, quantum systems are inevitably subject to significant uncertainties, including unknown initial states, imprecise physical parameters, and unmodeled environmental noise, all of which pose major challenges to robust quantum feedback control. This paper proposes a feedback stabilization strategy based on a reduced quantum filter that achieves robustness against time-varying Hamiltonian perturbations and additional dissipative effects, without requiring prior knowledge of the initial state or exact system parameters.

pmc-10577331.title: Non-tuberculous mycobacterial disease: progress and advances in the development of novel candidate and repurposed drugs
pmc-10577331.creator: Yuzhen Gu, Wenjuan Nie, Hairong Huang, Xia Yu
pmc-10577331.description: Non-tuberculous mycobacteria (NTM) are opportunistic pathogens that can infect all body tissues and organs. In particular, the lungs are the most commonly involved organ, with NTM pulmonary diseases causing serious health issues in patients with underlying lung disease. Moreover, NTM infections have been steadily increasing worldwide in recent years.

pmc-11674312.title: Development of a Japanese Version of the Parenting Sense of Competence Scale, and Examining the Structure of Japanese Mothers’ Parenting Self-Efficacy
pmc-11674312.creator: Tomomi Tanigo, Masayuki Endo, Kazutomo Ohashi, Matteo Fabris
pmc-11674312.description: Objective: Parenting self-efficacy (PSE) is an important factor in children’s development. Mothers’ PSE tends to be the lowest 1 month postpartum. A common measure of PSE is the Parenting Sense of Competence (PSOC) scale. However, no existing scale measures the PSE of Japanese mothers with newborns.

pmc-12532802.title: Multiport bidirectional converters for off board charging stations of electric vehicles
pmc-12532802.creator: Hazem H Mostafa, Amr M Ibrahim, Fathy Z Amer, Eman F Sawires
pmc-12532802.description: In this paper, two multi-port bi-directional converters are proposed to be utilized as off-board Electric Vehicles (EVs) charging station. Both converters are designed to integrate renewable energy along with grid power. High gain, three ports, and four modes of operation are the main advantages of these converters. The first mode is Photovoltaic-to-Vehicle (PV2V), the second is Grid-to-Vehicle (G2V).

pmc-13470709.title: Impact Angle–Velocity Interactions Governing Solid-Particle Erosion in Laser Powder Bed Fused AlSi10Mg
pmc-13470709.creator: Rashmi Saragur Nanjundaiah, Shrikantha Sasihithlu Rao, Praveenkumar K, Calvin Samuel S, T. Ram Prabhu, Katerina Skotnicova
pmc-13470709.description: This study investigates the erosive wear behavior of laser powder bed fused (LPBF) AlSi10Mg alloy samples subjected to different heat treatments, including T5 (direct aging), T6, SR (stress relieving), and as-built (AB) conditions. pmc-13474684.title: From in silico screening to experimental verification: Identification of novel umami peptides from tamarind (Tamarindus indica L.) seed proteins and their validation in enzymatic hydrolysates
pmc-13474684.creator: Sisi Huang, Shurui Li, Xiaoying Wang, Xuening Jiu, Shengbao Cai
pmc-13474684.description: Umami peptides are key contributors to food flavor enhancement. In this study, novel umami peptides from tamarind seed proteins were identified using an integrated strategy combining in silico screening and experimental validation. A virtual peptide library was screened based on physicochemical properties and bioactivity, yielding six candidates (VSDY, DGIDF, AKNVSDYL, YNDPHC, VPPD, and NDPHCQY).

pmc-13644119.title: Metabolic and functional analysis including repetitive antigen stimulation provides a more accurate assessment for CAR-T cell product quality and long-term functionality
pmc-13644119.creator: Beatriz Guijarro-Albaladejo, Belén Sierro-Martínez, Inmaculada Carrasco-Brocal, Paola Hernández-Díaz, María de la Rosa-Garrido, Raquel Muñoz-García, Jose Antonio Bejarano-García, Joan Mañé-Pujol, Patricia Alcalde-Mellado, Alfonso Rodríguez-Gil, Virginia Escamilla-Gómez, Maribel Lara-Chica, Cristina
pmc-13644119.description: BackgroundBCMA-directed CAR-T cell therapy has demonstrated remarkable clinical efficacy in multiple myeloma, but robust methods to evaluate product quality and predict long-term functionality remain underdeveloped. While immunophenotypic features of leukapheresis products correlate with clinical outcomes, the characterization of infused CAR-T cell products remains challenging and inconsistent across studies.
